This Week in the Bay

Tuesday–Sunday, September 8–13, 2026 · SF · East Bay · South Bay · North Bay

This is the week the season turns over. Last week the big calendars were empty; this week SFJAZZ, SF Opera, Berkeley Rep, Smuin, Center REP, the Presidio Theatre and the Stanford Theatre all open within four days of each other, and twelve pianos appear in the Botanical Garden. Underneath that, the small stuff is unusually good: three free-jazz elders in a Mission warehouse, a shuttered Chinatown banquet palace opened for one day, a 24-hour relay reading of Moby-Dick, and a mass scream at the Pacific. Use Day and Region to narrow.

🎹 Flower Piano, Sept 10–20 — 12 pianos, 55 acres 🎷 SFJAZZ opening week — Christian McBride 🎭 Bay Area Theatre Week, Sept 10–20 (code BATW2026) 🐋 24-hour Moby-Dick marathon, Sat noon→Sun noon 🌲 Sunny, 68–70°F, no fog — telescopes are on

The Top 5 This Week

Five picks across all categories — chosen for rarity, variety, and things that genuinely will not happen again.
01 · EXPERIMENTAL MUSIC

Heart Trio — William Parker, Hamid Drake, Cooper-Moore

Fri Sep 11, 8pm (doors 7:30) · The Lab, Mission, SF · $40

Three elders of American free music who have played together for thirty years, entirely improvised — on guembri, shakuhachi, duduk, ashimba and a harp Cooper-Moore built from a hoe handle. One Bay Area date, in a 100-capacity room.

02 · NEW MUSIC IN A LANDMARK

Del Sol Quartet on Angel Island

Sat Sep 12, from 11:30am · Immigration Station Detention Barracks, Tiburon · $5

Two world premieres performed inside the barracks where Chinese immigrants were detained for weeks — Josiah Catalan’s piece woven with live slam poetry, and Dante de Silva’s “Aposematic.” Five dollars, a ferry ride, and a room with carved poems still in the walls.

03 · MUSIC OUTDOORS · ★ 48 HILLS

Flower Piano — 12 pianos, 55 acres

Opens Thu Sep 10, daily through Sep 20 · SF Botanical Garden · FREE for SF residents / $18

Twelve pianos hidden through the Botanical Garden for eleven days, 130 scheduled sets and open play for anyone who sits down. This weekend alone: Lavay Smith, Tango No. 9, SF Ballet School dancing on the Great Meadow, and Symphony musicians on Sunday.

04 · LITERARY ENDURANCE SPORT

The 24-Hour Moby-Dick Marathon

Sat Sep 12 noon → Sun Sep 13 noon · SF Maritime Museum, Aquatic Park · FREE

Melville read cover to cover, without stopping, by relays of volunteers — inside a 1939 Streamline Moderne bathhouse on the beach. Come for one chapter or stay the whole night. Co-presented with Litquake; you can sign up to read.

05 · RARE ACCESS · ★ KQED

Empress of China — open house

Sat Sep 12, 11am–4pm (program 1pm) · 838 Grant Ave, Chinatown, SF · FREE

The 1966 banquet palace that held three generations of Chinatown weddings has been shut since 2016. It reopens for one day under community ownership: Buddhist blessings, First Nations drumming, a lion dance, and the chance to simply walk in.

Galleries, Openings & Artist Spaces

12 openings

This is the fall gallery season’s opening week. Roughly 35 receptions land across two nights: Thursday in SoMa, Chinatown and Potrero; Saturday in Dogpatch, Oakland and on Sutter St. Fraenkel and Jessica Silverman both reopen from summer closure on Thursday. Wear comfortable shoes and pick a corridor.

How this was built

Every source row in sources.md was scanned across fifteen parallel sweeps — aggregators, museums, galleries, literary, immersive, oddities, lectures, classical, theater, cinema, dance, markets, cultural centers, casual/spa and critics’ outlets — then filtered against the taste profile and ranked by hand. Times were read off each venue’s own event page rather than an aggregator grid wherever one existed. Restaurant pairings come from the 480-spot fit-ranked database in this repo.

Verify before you go

⚠ SF Opera’s opening night is at risk. AFM Local 6 stated on Aug 27 that the orchestra “will not be able to perform on Opening Night, September 12, unless management has reached a fair contract”; the Opera Ball has already been postponed to November. Check before travelling. Telescope nights are clear-sky only — the forecast is good (sunny, 68–69°F, no fog, new moon Sep 11), but Chabot closes its refractors above ~90% humidity, so check the same evening. Sold out: BAMPFA’s Thursday Alice Diop screening and Saturday Taxi Driver; Bryan Stevenson at City Arts; Clio’s The Nerd Reich; Kamasi Washington’s 7pm set; Lick Observatory often sells out. Unconfirmed: the JCCCNC kabuki class date (the program page implies third Thursdays); East Bay Bike Party’s theme and start point drop on Instagram ~24h ahead; the Angel Island sunset-cruise dates should be confirmed on the operator’s calendar. Closed days: SFMOMA Wed; BAMPFA and Computer History Mon/Tue; Asian Art Tue/Wed; Hiller Aviation Sun; Archimedes Banya Tue; the Exploratorium’s Tactile Dome is out for maintenance Sep 8–28.

Deliberately left out

EDM and DJ club nights, arena and stadium shows, sports, bar crawls, brunch-as-event, networking mixers and expos — including the Bay Area Theatre Week kick-off mixers, a large block of free comedy showcases, and the touring Oddities & Curiosities Expo, which reads well but is an expo. The 9/11 Truth Film Festival at the Grand Lake was dropped for its conspiracy framing. Pride- and identity-framed programming was deprioritised rather than removed, per the taste profile.

Just outside the window

Worth booking now: SF Open Studios opens with ArtLaunch Sep 18 and runs weekends to Oct 25; the Fort Mason Night Market and Off the Grid Fridays return Sep 18; Hubba Hubba Revue’s 20th-anniversary superspectacular and the Haight-Ashbury Street Fair are both Sep 20; “Dear San Francisco” resumes at Club Fugazi Sep 17; SF Chinatown’s Autumn Moon Festival is Sep 19–20; the Bay Area Chuseok Festival is Sep 26; Cal Performances opens Sep 25; and Litquake runs Oct 3–24.
